long_biography.plain_text:
The son of a Liverpool docker, Hargreaves left school at 14 and learned retail by selling discounted clothing from market stalls. He developed those lessons into Jaymax, an early chain of town-centre shops, before a visit to the United States showed him the potential of out-of-town warehouse retail. In 1985 he opened the first Matalan store near Preston, combining direct purchasing, low-cost locations and value-focused clothing and homeware.

Matalan expanded rapidly and floated on the London Stock Exchange. Hargreaves remained its largest shareholder and executive chairman, then led an £817 million take-private transaction. He later stepped back from management, and a 2023 debt-for-equity recapitalisation ended the family's control. His public identity and wealth nevertheless remain rooted in the retail platform he created.
